title: Euler Product Form of the Basel Problem
description: The infinite product over primes ∏_p (1-p⁻²)⁻¹ equals π²/6, connecting the Basel sum to prime numbers via Euler's product formula.

overview.historicalContext:
Euler made two groundbreaking discoveries about infinite series in the 1730s. In 1734, he solved the Basel Problem (posed by Pietro Mengoli in 1644 and unsolved for ~90 years): ∑_{n=1}^∞ 1/n² = π²/6. His proof used the infinite product factorization of sin(πx)/πx, a technique that was later made rigorous by Weierstrass. The Basel result connected the sum of reciprocal squares — a purely arithmetic object — to π, which was deeply surprising to contemporaries.

In 1737, Euler discovered the product representation ζ(s) = ∏_p (1-p⁻ˢ)⁻¹, where the product runs over all prime numbers. The key insight was to expand each factor as a geometric series: (1-p⁻ˢ)⁻¹ = 1 + p⁻ˢ + p⁻²ˢ + ..., then observe that multiplying over all primes generates exactly the terms n⁻ˢ for all natural numbers n, by the fundamental theorem of arithmetic (unique prime factorization).

Combining these two results at s=2 gives ∏_p (1-p⁻²)⁻¹ = π²/6, connecting the distribution of primes to π. The reciprocal ∏_p (1-1/p²) = 6/π² ≈ 0.6079 has a beautiful probabilistic interpretation (Cesàro 1881): it equals the probability that two randomly chosen positive integers are coprime. This formalization captures all three equivalent forms (tprod, HasProd, Tendsto) of this identity using Mathlib's `riemannZeta_eulerProduct` family and `riemannZeta_two`.
overview.problemStatement: Prove that the infinite product ∏_p (1-p⁻²)⁻¹ over all primes p equals π²/6.
overview.text: The Euler product form of the Basel Problem: ∏_p (1-p⁻²)⁻¹ = π²/6.
overview.proofStrategy:
Direct combination of two Mathlib theorems:
1. riemannZeta_eulerProduct_tprod: ∏_p (1-p^{-s})⁻¹ = ζ(s) for Re(s) > 1
2. riemannZeta_two: ζ(2) = π²/6

Substituting s = 2 and chaining the equalities gives the result.
keyInsights: The proof is a 2-line combination of existing Mathlib infrastructure — the power of formal libraries.
Three equivalent formulations capture different aspects: tprod (value), HasProd (convergence proof), Tendsto (partial product convergence).
The identity ∏_p (1-1/p²) = 6/π² ≈ 0.6079 gives the density of coprime pairs among integers.
Euler's original argument expanded each (1-p⁻ˢ)⁻¹ as a geometric series and used unique factorization.

The condition Re(s) > 1 is essential for convergence: at s=1 the product diverges (harmonic series), reflecting the infinitude of primes. The Euler product is the key analytic tool connecting the multiplicative structure of integers (primes) to additive structure (sums). The Riemann hypothesis is essentially a question about the zeros of this product as a function of complex s.

sections.title: Historical Context and Euler's Argument
sections.summary: Explains Euler's 1737 product argument and the coprimality probability interpretation.
sections.mathContext: Euler's argument uses unique factorization: ∏_p (1 + p^{-s} + p^{-2s} + ...) = ∑_n n^{-s}. At s=2: ∏_p (p²-1)/p² = 6/π² ≈ 0.6079.

conclusion.summary: A fully verified proof that ∏_p (1-p⁻²)⁻¹ = π²/6, combining the Euler product formula with the Basel identity. Zero axioms, zero sorries.
conclusion.implications: Connects Euler's product formula to the zeta function, establishing a foundational bridge between analytic and algebraic number theory.
